facts.text: Amandari was designed after a traditional Balinese village on the edge of the Ayung River Gorge.
facts.excerpt: Amandari was designed after a traditional Balinese village on the verdant lip of the Ayung River Gorge.

facts.text: The resort is close to the artistic centre of Ubud.
facts.excerpt: Close to the artistic centre of Ubud, this place of peace invites exploration of Bali’s cultural heart.

facts.text: Amandari sits in Kedewatan village, north of Ubud centre.
facts.excerpt: Kedewatan village, a traditional little gem north of Ubud center

facts.text: The transfer from the airport is a one and a half hour drive.
facts.excerpt: A one and a half hour drive

facts.text: Amandari claims the first infinity pool in Bali.
facts.excerpt: It claims the first infinity pool in Bali

facts.text: Amandari was the first luxury hotel in Ubud and the second Aman.
facts.excerpt: the very first luxury hotel in Ubud and second-ever Aman

facts.text: The resort does not use golf carts to shuttle guests around.
facts.excerpt: Amandari is a rare Bali resort that doesn’t use golf carts to shuttle guests from place to place

facts.text: Suites have no TV on the wall; one is available on request.
facts.excerpt: There was no TV hanging on the wall, or anywhere for that matter. (They are available by request.)

facts.text: Every suite has a sunken outdoor marble tub large enough for two.
facts.excerpt: plus a sunken outdoor marble tub large enough for two—a hallmark of each suite

facts.text: Every suite has a private bale, a small open-air pavilion.
facts.excerpt: a small open-air pavilion with a roof and bamboo or wood floor. Each suite has one, regardless of whether it has a pool.

facts.text: The resort has one restaurant, called The Restaurant.
facts.excerpt: There’s but one restaurant here and it’s simply called The Restaurant.

facts.text: Amandari offers a Ngejot Balinese Feast at The Restaurant at dinner time.
facts.excerpt: Upholding this tradition, Amandari offers Ngejot Balinese Feast at The Restaurant during dinner time

facts.text: Stays include daily breakfast and daily traditional afternoon tea.
Guests can join a daily Balinese dance and rindik class with children from Kedewatan village.
facts.excerpt: Daily Balinese dance and rindik class with children from Kedewatan village

facts.text: The spa has two open-air treatment bales surrounded by lotus ponds.
facts.excerpt: Two open-air treatment bales surrounded by lotus ponds

facts.text: The resort has a tennis court with all equipment provided.
facts.excerpt: Tennis court with all equipment provided

facts.text: Guests can go with a tour guide to Tirta Empul for an early-morning melukat purification ceremony before it opens to the public.
facts.excerpt: Amandari guests can opt to go with a tour guide to the nearby water temple Tirta Empul for an early-morning melukat purification ceremony before it opens to the public.
Amandari’s spa is small but bliss-inducing.

facts.text: Reaching most of the resort, including The Restaurant, requires climbing steps.
facts.excerpt: reaching most everything else, including The Restaurant, requires climbing steps.
